title.source: FriXion改過的字，六十度後還留哪一版？｜品牌故事
title.text: Your FriXion edits: which version survives 60°C? | Brand Stories

description.source:
一支能寫、消、再寫的筆，到底把什麼留在紙上？跟著FriXion的一筆修改，看記憶型變色材料、微膠囊小型化與量產，如何接到現代使用者的草稿。低溫回色與不能完整復原的界線，決定這張紙應該選哪種筆。歷史依原廠及開發者回顧歸屬，匿名概念插圖不作同期現場或零售配方剖面。

description.text:
What does a pen that writes, erases and writes again actually leave on paper? Follow one FriXion correction through color-change materials with memory, smaller microcapsules and mass production, and into a user's draft today. Color returning in the cold—and the limits of full recovery—help determine which pen belongs on that page. Historical accounts are attributed to the maker and developers. Anonymous concept illustrations do not depict documented contemporary scenes or a cutaway of the retail ink formula.

c15r1h02: PILOT的營業人員後來回憶，日本一家文具專門店試賣時，
顧客親手寫，接著拿膠擦去擦。
c15r1h03: 我覺得，這個動作比廣告更難交代：
筆尖剛留下的東西，怎麼交給另一端處理？
c15r1h05: 追過三十多年的變色研究，看它怎麼走到你手裡。
c15r1a01: 想像你正在改一份草稿，先用這支筆劃下一道線；
真正要擦之前，手得先停一下。
c15a02c1: 原廠側欄談到膠擦選材時，說要有彈性，
還要耐磨；膠擦本身也得承受一次次使用。
c15r1a03: 如果你只看見擦這個動作，
很容易把它當成另一種橡皮；它究竟怎麼讓顏色不見？
c15r1a09: 我喜歡這裡的省事：修改不必搬到紙張的旁邊，
也不用另外拉一條線，替新內容找位置。
c15r1a10: 但如果只是把顏色藏起來，
為什麼你放開手之後，舊線沒有立刻再冒出來？
c15r1a12: 每個膠囊裡，裝著決定顏色的成分、
使它顯色的成分，還有調整變色溫度的材料。
c15r1a13: 這三種工作，被放在同一個小空間裡；
光有決定黑、紅等顏色的染料，就能顯色嗎？
c15r1b06: 原廠回顧早期材料，升溫時慢慢變色，
放著又會回色，連改變的分界也不夠清楚。
c15r1b08: 這一型降到接近那個溫度以下，也很快回色；
變得俐落了，卻還留不住一次改動。
c15r1b09: 我覺得這才是關鍵：要讓你停手後的修改不馬上翻回去，
c15r1b10: 開發接著轉向記憶型：加熱變過色，
必須再冷到另一個更低的設定溫度，才會回色。
c15r1b13: 公司記錄一九八八年能在約二十度的溫差間保持色態；
再拉開，該怎麼找調整劑？
c15r1b14: 那個差距，來自調整劑的選擇；千賀回憶，
起步時用的是已經存在的物質。
c15r1b15: 後來，團隊自己製作超過一千種原創化合物，
尋找想要的變色溫度調整劑。
c15r1b16: 但要把這些材料交到你寫字的那一端，
光把溫度範圍拉開，還過不了筆尖。
c15r1c01: 依原廠回顧，初期膠囊直徑約十到十五微米；
到了記憶型階段，縮到五到十微米。
c15r1c04: 我沒想到，膠囊縮小，膜卻變薄、
更容易破裂；除了薄，墨水還會帶來什麼？
c15r1c06: 而膠囊進入墨水，還會碰到溶劑與添加物；
千賀說，其中許多與膠囊相容性不好。
c15r1c07: 所以膜不只要夠強，還得耐受這些成分；
團隊連包覆的方法與條件，也一起研究。
c15r1c08: 二〇〇〇年代初，膠囊縮到約二到三微米，
能用於筆具墨水；先走出哪支筆？
c15r1c10: 它寫下黑色的筆跡，再用筆帽上的專用膠擦摩擦，
黑色會變成另一種顏色。
c15r1c11: 可是，如果你想改掉一個錯字，換一種顏色，
還是把舊筆跡留在原來的位置。
c15r1c12: 歐洲子公司的行銷人員看見這支筆後，
向開發負責人提出：能不能從有色，變成透明？
c15r1c14: 公司以法國的用筆情境解釋：
某些墨水可用消字液處理，原筆還能接著寫嗎？
c15r1c18: 研發還有日常溫差要處理；回顧記下零至四十度的溫域，
跨出去，色態就可能跟著變。
c15r1c19: 後來的新調整劑，把這個歷史研發範圍，
拉到零下二十至六十五度，相隔八十五度。
c15r1d01: 原廠回顧，二〇〇四年決定商品化；
專案要讓工廠大量做出與燒杯同品質的墨水。
c15r1d03: 開場那批等著離開燒杯的膠囊，
到了千賀的量產回憶裡，數量是五百公斤。
c15r1d04: 這一關得建立穩定生產膠囊的技術；
放大以後，還多出了哪些小燒杯沒有的問題？
c15r1d05: 其中一項，是膠囊做成墨水後，會出現分離或劣化；
不是膠囊能做出來，事情就結束。
c15r1d06: 墨水開發人員得與產品設計、
生產設備及企畫合作，把這些問題一起處理。
c15r1d07: 我覺得，這比單獨找到會消色的材料更吃力；
別人手上沒有成功的燒杯，要怎麼買到它？
c15r1d08: 原廠把這段跨部門合作，記為越過量產難關的過程；
c15r1d10: 開場那次寫與擦的試賣，重點正是親手體驗；
營業的鈴木直之回憶，顧客看見消色，接著有人購買。
c15r1d12: 二〇〇七年三月，這支筆在日本上市；
紙上的修改，開始有了可直接買到的工具。
c15r1d14: 當初為了讓修改留下而拉開的溫差，
碰到另一端的冷或熱，還會怎麼改動這一頁？
c15r1e01: 先把草稿放回日常環境。現行說明列出，陽光直射、
發熱機材或熱水杯附近，都可能讓筆跡變淡或無色。
c15r1e02: 開場擔心的那一頁，若真的受熱消色，
原廠另有一條回答：冷卻能讓顏色開始回來。
c15r1e03: 說明先把限制擺明：不能保證顏色確實恢復；
那它把開始回色，放在哪裡？
c15r1e04: 它把開始回色，寫在零下十度以下；
到了零下二十度前後，則有完整回色的特性。
c15r1e07: 原廠明示，重疊寫過的內容，會一起回色；
先前擦掉的舊筆跡，也可能夾在新內容裡。
c15r1e08: 而用摩擦擦過的筆跡，說明直接寫不能完整回色；
把紙冷下來，不能當成復原鍵。
c15r1e09: 若極端高溫或強紫外線直射，
已把墨水成分破壞，原廠也說顏色無法恢復。
c15r1e11: 原廠的長期保存回答沒有這樣說：避開前面那段高溫，
可達到其他染料型凝膠墨水同程度的保存。
c15r1e12: 它也保留紫外線會使筆跡逐漸褪色的條件，
沒有替每一張紙訂下保證年限。
c15r1e13: 所以，你要交出去的如果是不能消字的證書或地址，
就得把筆換掉；這些用途在原廠的禁用範圍。
c15e13c1: 原廠列出，粗糙紙或和紙的表面，
可能在摩擦時受損；紙面有塗層，也可能比較難寫。
c15r1e15: 開頭那個問題，我的答案是：這支筆把顏色的狀態交給溫度，
留給你的，是能修改、也得選用途的一頁。

lines.source: 你剛改好的一頁筆記，若紙張到了六十度，還能留下哪一版？
lines.text: You have just corrected a page of notes. If the paper reaches 60°C, which version will remain?

lines.source: PILOT的營業人員後來回憶，日本一家文具專門店試賣時，顧客親手寫，接著拿膠擦去擦。
lines.text: A PILOT sales representative later recalled a trial sale at a Japanese stationery specialty shop: customers wrote with the pen themselves, then rubbed the marks with its eraser.

lines.source: 我覺得，這個動作比廣告更難交代：筆尖剛留下的東西，怎麼交給另一端處理？
lines.text: To me, that action is harder to explain than an advertisement: how does one end deal with what the nib has just left behind?

lines.source: 它的背後，還有等著離開小燒杯的一批膠囊。
lines.text: Behind it is also a batch of capsules waiting to leave a small beaker.

lines.source: 而寫完的那張紙，溫度也有機會再插手。
lines.text: And temperature may have another say in what happens to the finished page.

lines.source: 跟著FriXion的一筆修改，追過三十多年的變色研究，看它怎麼走到你手裡。
lines.text: Follow a single FriXion correction through more than 30 years of color-change research to see how it reached your hand.

lines.source: 同一支筆寫、消、再寫，究竟把什麼留在紙上，又把什麼交給了溫度？
lines.text: One pen writes, erases and writes again. What does it leave on paper, and what does it leave up to temperature?

lines.source: 想像你正在改一份草稿，先用這支筆劃下一道線；真正要擦之前，手得先停一下。
lines.text: Imagine correcting a draft. Draw a line with this pen first; before you actually erase it, your hand needs to pause.

lines.source: 現行說明要求，等筆跡乾了，再讓附屬的專用膠擦接觸紙面。
lines.text: The current instructions say to wait for the ink to dry before touching the paper with the attached special eraser.

lines.source: 接觸紙面的那塊材料，又是怎麼選出來的？
lines.text: How was the material that touches the paper chosen?

lines.source: 原廠側欄談到膠擦選材時，說要有彈性，還要耐磨；膠擦本身也得承受一次次使用。
lines.text: In a sidebar on eraser materials, the maker says it needs elasticity and wear resistance; the eraser itself must withstand repeated use.

lines.source: 如果你只看見擦這個動作，很容易把它當成另一種橡皮；它究竟怎麼讓顏色不見？
lines.text: If you only see the rubbing action, it is easy to think of this as another rubber eraser. How does it make the color disappear?

lines.source: 專用膠擦摩擦產熱，讓紙上的墨水變得無色；這種消色不會產生消字屑。
lines.text: Rubbing with the special eraser generates heat, making the ink on the paper colorless. This decoloring produces no erasing debris.

lines.source: 開場問的那個溫度，正是現行墨水說明所列的消色門檻。
lines.text: The temperature in our opening question is the decoloring threshold listed in the current ink explanation.

lines.source: 所以，剛才那個位置接下來能做什麼？
lines.text: So what can happen next in that same spot?

lines.source: 你把筆轉回來，在消色處重新落筆，同一個位置就能寫上新的內容。
lines.text: You turn the pen back around and write where the color disappeared, putting new content in the same place.

lines.source: 我喜歡這裡的省事：修改不必搬到紙張的旁邊，也不用另外拉一條線，替新內容找位置。
lines.text: I like the convenience: you do not have to move the correction to the side of the page or draw another line to make room for the new content.

lines.source: 但如果只是把顏色藏起來，為什麼你放開手之後，舊線沒有立刻再冒出來？
lines.text: But if the color is merely hidden, why does the old line not immediately reappear when you let go?

lines.source: 這個問題，得縮到筆跡裡去看。擔任色材的，是一顆顆微膠囊。
lines.text: To answer that, we need to zoom into the marks. Tiny microcapsules serve as the color material.

lines.source: 每個膠囊裡，裝著決定顏色的成分、使它顯色的成分，還有調整變色溫度的材料。
lines.text: Each capsule contains a component that determines the color, one that makes it develop, and material that adjusts the color-change temperature.

lines.source: 這三種工作，被放在同一個小空間裡；光有決定黑、紅等顏色的染料，就能顯色嗎？
lines.text: Those three jobs fit into one tiny space. Can a dye that determines black, red and other colors develop color on its own?

lines.source: 開發者千賀邦行解釋，那種染料與顯色劑結合，才會顯出黑、紅等顏色。
lines.text: Developer Senga explains that the dye shows black, red and other colors only when it combines with a color developer.

lines.source: 而調整劑會介入這個組合，決定溫度變到哪裡時，顏色跟著換一個狀態。
lines.text: The temperature-adjusting agent acts on that combination, determining the temperature at which the color changes state.

lines.source: 要讓這道舊線維持修改，調整劑在開發時，先遇上什麼麻煩？
lines.text: To keep that old line corrected, what difficulty did developers first face with the adjusting agent?

lines.source: 原廠回顧早期材料，升溫時慢慢變色，放著又會回色，連改變的分界也不夠清楚。
lines.text: Looking back at the early material, the maker says its color changed slowly as it warmed and returned when left alone; even the transition was not sharply defined.

lines.source: 團隊把焦點放在調整劑，先做成高感度型：到某個溫度，顏色迅速改變。
lines.text: The team focused on the adjusting agent and first made a high-sensitivity type: its color changed quickly at a certain temperature.

lines.source: 這一型降到接近那個溫度以下，也很快回色；變得俐落了，卻還留不住一次改動。
lines.text: This type also regained color quickly when cooled below a point near that temperature. The change was sharper, but a correction still would not stay put.

lines.source: 我覺得這才是關鍵：要讓你停手後的修改不馬上翻回去，兩個溫度能不能分開？
lines.text: To me, this is the key: to keep your correction from immediately reversing after you stop, could those two temperatures be separated?

lines.source: 開發接著轉向記憶型：加熱變過色，必須再冷到另一個更低的設定溫度，才會回色。
lines.text: Development then turned to a memory type: after heat changed its color, it would regain color only when cooled to another, lower preset temperature.

lines.source: 早期記憶型，曾把變色與回色的兩端隔開多遠？
lines.text: How far apart were the color-change and color-return points in the early memory type?

lines.source: 公司記錄一九八八年能在約二十度的溫差間保持色態；再拉開，該怎麼找調整劑？
lines.text: The company records that in 1988 it could retain its color state across a gap of about 20 degrees. To widen that gap, how would they find the adjusting agent?

lines.source: 那個差距，來自調整劑的選擇；千賀回憶，起步時用的是已經存在的物質。
lines.text: The gap depended on the choice of adjusting agent. Senga recalls that they started with substances that already existed.

lines.source: 後來，團隊自己製作超過一千種原創化合物，尋找想要的變色溫度調整劑。
lines.text: Later, the team made more than 1,000 original compounds themselves, seeking agents that would set the desired color-change temperatures.

lines.source: 但要把這些材料交到你寫字的那一端，光把溫度範圍拉開，還過不了筆尖。
lines.text: But getting those materials to the end you write with required more than a wider temperature range. They still had to get through the nib.

lines.source: 那些負責變色的小膠囊，當時大到什麼程度？
lines.text: How large were those little color-changing capsules at the time?

lines.source: 依原廠回顧，初期膠囊直徑約十到十五微米；到了記憶型階段，縮到五到十微米。
lines.text: According to the maker's retrospective, the early capsules were about 10 to 15 micrometers in diameter, shrinking to five to 10 micrometers at the memory-type stage.

lines.source: 可是，墨水要從原子筆尖細小的間隙順暢出去，那時的膠囊仍然太大。
lines.text: Yet those capsules were still too large for ink to flow smoothly through the tiny gaps in a ballpoint tip.

lines.source: 我沒想到，膠囊縮小，膜卻變薄、更容易破裂；除了薄，墨水還會帶來什麼？
lines.text: I had not expected smaller capsules to have thinner, more fragile shells. Beyond thinness, what challenge would the ink bring?

lines.source: 而膠囊進入墨水，還會碰到溶劑與添加物；千賀說，其中許多與膠囊相容性不好。
lines.text: Once mixed into ink, the capsules also encountered solvents and additives. Senga says many were poorly compatible with the capsules.

lines.source: 所以膜不只要夠強，還得耐受這些成分；團隊連包覆的方法與條件，也一起研究。
lines.text: So the shell had to be strong and withstand those ingredients. The team also studied the encapsulation methods and conditions.

lines.source: 二〇〇〇年代初，膠囊縮到約二到三微米，能用於筆具墨水；先走出哪支筆？
lines.text: In the early 2000s, capsules shrank to about two to three micrometers, making them usable in pen ink. Which pen came first?

lines.source: 筆尖這一關跨過後，二〇〇二年出現了一支名叫ILLUSION的裝飾筆。
lines.text: After overcoming the nib problem, a decorating pen called ILLUSION appeared in 2002.

lines.source: 它寫下黑色的筆跡，再用筆帽上的專用膠擦摩擦，黑色會變成另一種顏色。
lines.text: It wrote in black; rubbing with the special eraser on the cap changed the black into another color.

lines.source: 可是，如果你想改掉一個錯字，換一種顏色，還是把舊筆跡留在原來的位置。
lines.text: But if you wanted to correct a misspelled word, changing its color still left the old writing in the same place.

lines.source: 歐洲子公司的行銷人員看見這支筆後，向開發負責人提出：能不能從有色，變成透明？
lines.text: After seeing this pen, a marketing employee at the European subsidiary asked the development lead: could it go from colored to transparent?

lines.source: 公司以法國的用筆情境解釋：某些墨水可用消字液處理，原筆還能接著寫嗎？
lines.text: The company explains this through pen use in France: certain inks could be treated with an ink eradicator, but could the original pen then write there again?

lines.source: 但消字液浸過的地方，不能再由原來那支筆重寫，得另拿一支專用筆。
lines.text: Where the eradicator had soaked in, the original pen could not rewrite. You needed another, dedicated pen.

lines.source: 研發還有日常溫差要處理；回顧記下零至四十度的溫域，跨出去，色態就可能跟著變。
lines.text: Development also had to address everyday temperature changes. The retrospective records a range from zero to 40°C; outside it, the color state could change.

lines.source: 後來的新調整劑，把這個歷史研發範圍，拉到零下二十至六十五度，相隔八十五度。
lines.text: A later adjusting agent extended that historical development range to minus 20 to 65°C, a gap of 85 degrees.

lines.source: 小燒杯裡有了材料成果，若要把它做成商品，大量生產時得守住什麼？
lines.text: The material worked in a small beaker. To make it a product, what had to stay consistent in mass production?

lines.source: 原廠回顧，二〇〇四年決定商品化；專案要讓工廠大量做出與燒杯同品質的墨水。
lines.text: The maker recalls deciding on commercialization in 2004. The project had to produce ink at the factory in large quantities, with the same quality as in the beaker.

lines.source: 你若只看膠囊這一步，穩定生產的量，得有多大？
lines.text: Looking just at the capsule step, how much had to be produced reliably?

lines.source: 開場那批等著離開燒杯的膠囊，到了千賀的量產回憶裡，數量是五百公斤。
lines.text: The capsules waiting to leave the beaker in our opening amount to 500 kilograms in Senga's recollection of mass production.

lines.source: 這一關得建立穩定生產膠囊的技術；放大以後，還多出了哪些小燒杯沒有的問題？
lines.text: This required technology for stable capsule production. What problems arose on scaling up that a small beaker did not have?

lines.source: 其中一項，是膠囊做成墨水後，會出現分離或劣化；不是膠囊能做出來，事情就結束。
lines.text: One was separation or deterioration after the capsules were made into ink. Being able to make capsules did not finish the job.

lines.source: 墨水開發人員得與產品設計、生產設備及企畫合作，把這些問題一起處理。
lines.text: Ink developers had to work with product design, production equipment and planning to deal with these problems together.

lines.source: 我覺得，這比單獨找到會消色的材料更吃力；別人手上沒有成功的燒杯，要怎麼買到它？
lines.text: To me, that is harder than finding a material that loses color. Other people do not have that successful beaker—how can they buy it?

lines.source: 原廠把這段跨部門合作，記為越過量產難關的過程；二〇〇六年，FriXion先在歐洲上市。
lines.text: The maker describes this collaboration across departments as the process of overcoming mass-production obstacles. In 2006, FriXion launched first in Europe.

lines.source: 產品走到日本以前，營業團隊先讓文具店顧客拿筆；那隻手試過以後呢？
lines.text: Before bringing the product to Japan, the sales team put pens in stationery-shop customers' hands. What happened after they tried them?

lines.source: 開場那次寫與擦的試賣，重點正是親手體驗；營業的鈴木直之回憶，顧客看見消色，接著有人購買。
lines.text: The trial sale with writing and erasing in our opening centered on hands-on experience. Sales representative Suzuki recalls that customers saw the color disappear, and some then bought the pen.

lines.source: 二〇〇七年三月，這支筆在日本上市；紙上的修改，開始有了可直接買到的工具。
lines.text: In March 2007, the pen launched in Japan. There was now a tool you could buy directly for corrections on paper.

lines.source: 當初為了讓修改留下而拉開的溫差，碰到另一端的冷或熱，還會怎麼改動這一頁？
lines.text: That temperature gap was widened to keep corrections in place. When heat or cold reaches the other end, how else might it change this page?

lines.source: 先把草稿放回日常環境。現行說明列出，陽光直射、發熱機材或熱水杯附近，都可能讓筆跡變淡或無色。
lines.text: First, return the draft to everyday surroundings. Current instructions say direct sunlight, heat-generating equipment or a nearby cup of hot water can make the writing faint or colorless.

lines.source: 開場擔心的那一頁，若真的受熱消色，原廠另有一條回答：冷卻能讓顏色開始回來。
lines.text: If the page we worried about at the start really does lose color from heat, the maker offers another answer: cooling can start bringing the color back.

lines.source: 說明先把限制擺明：不能保證顏色確實恢復；那它把開始回色，放在哪裡？
lines.text: The explanation states a limit first: definite color recovery is not guaranteed. So where does it put the start of recoloring?

lines.source: 它把開始回色，寫在零下十度以下；到了零下二十度前後，則有完整回色的特性。
lines.text: It says recoloring begins below minus 10°C, with the characteristic of full recoloring at around minus 20°C.

lines.source: 我更想知道，重寫過的那個位置，低溫會替你挑出最新的一版嗎？
lines.text: What I want to know is this: where you rewrote, will the cold select the latest version for you?

lines.source: 原廠明示，重疊寫過的內容，會一起回色；先前擦掉的舊筆跡，也可能夾在新內容裡。
lines.text: The maker explicitly says overlapping writing regains color together. Old marks erased earlier may appear among the new content.

lines.source: 而用摩擦擦過的筆跡，說明直接寫不能完整回色；把紙冷下來，不能當成復原鍵。
lines.text: For writing rubbed out by friction, the instructions directly say its color cannot return completely. Cooling the paper is no undo button.

lines.source: 若極端高溫或強紫外線直射，已把墨水成分破壞，原廠也說顏色無法恢復。
lines.text: If extreme heat or intense direct ultraviolet light has damaged the ink's components, the maker also says the color cannot be restored.

lines.source: 那是不是所有這種筆跡，都註定很快看不見？
lines.text: Does that mean all writing of this kind is destined to disappear quickly?

lines.source: 原廠的長期保存回答沒有這樣說：避開前面那段高溫，可達到其他染料型凝膠墨水同程度的保存。
lines.text: The maker's answer on long-term storage does not say that. Avoiding the high temperatures mentioned earlier allows preservation comparable to other dye-based gel inks.

lines.source: 它也保留紫外線會使筆跡逐漸褪色的條件，沒有替每一張紙訂下保證年限。
lines.text: It also retains the condition that ultraviolet light gradually fades the writing, without guaranteeing a lifespan for every sheet.

lines.source: 所以，你要交出去的如果是不能消字的證書或地址，就得把筆換掉；這些用途在原廠的禁用範圍。
lines.text: So if what you must hand over is a certificate or an address where writing must not disappear, change pens. The maker prohibits these uses.

lines.source: 即使留作草稿，你手裡的紙面，也適合這樣來回摩擦嗎？
lines.text: Even if it stays a draft, is the paper in your hand suited to this repeated rubbing?

lines.source: 原廠列出，粗糙紙或和紙的表面，可能在摩擦時受損；紙面有塗層，也可能比較難寫。
lines.text: The maker lists rough paper and Japanese washi as surfaces that may be damaged by friction; coated paper may also be harder to write on.

lines.source: 開頭那個問題，我的答案是：這支筆把顏色的狀態交給溫度，留給你的，是能修改、也得選用途的一頁。
lines.text: My answer to our opening question is this: the pen leaves the color's state up to temperature. It leaves you a page you can edit, but whose purpose you must choose.

lines.source: 留言分享，你最常拿這種筆改哪一頁，是行程、草稿，還是自己的筆記。
lines.text: Tell us in the comments which page you most often correct with this kind of pen: a schedule, a draft or your own notes.

lines.source: 想看熟悉的物品，怎麼把材料的取捨交到你手裡，歡迎訂閱品牌故事。
lines.text: To see how familiar objects put choices about materials into your hands, subscribe to Brand Stories.
